enemy-003-chestburster.method: Manual per-pose visual measurement of the ventral cervical/anterior-trunk root, projected vertically onto the complete source lower bound including extraction guard. Source images inspected at original dimensions with a 50px cell-relative QA grid, then each proposed landmark and floor projection inspected again with temporary cyan markers. No source image edits, no inferred root from tail bounding-box center.
enemy-003-chestburster.measurementLimit: Manual source-pixel measurements with declared uncertainty; hashes bind provenance only and do not certify canon fidelity or motion quality.
enemy-003-chestburster.baselinePolicy: anchor.y equals each complete extraction sourceBounds[3], which already preserves the bottom transparent guard; no per-frame image scaling and no skeleton or new frame synthesis.

frames.evidence: Prone pose: ventral cervical junction directly behind the skull, not the long tail midpoint. Floor is the complete preserved pose lower bound.
Neck rising: root at the lower forebody bend where the horizontal trunk turns upward; head rise remains above the root.
Higher neck: lower ventral bend under the raised cervical column, preserving the upward head movement.
Neck fully raised: lower forebody turn at ground contact, not the skull center.
Second-row raised pose: lower upright forebody bend; coordinates subtract the nominal row origin y=444.
Neck lowering: ventral cervical base where the rising neck joins the horizontal trunk; tail spill remains irrelevant to root placement.
Low neck: ventral cervical junction behind the skull, preserving the short head lift.
Return to prone: ventral neck/forebody junction, consistent with idle frame0 rather than whole-silhouette centering.
Prone forward body: cervical ring immediately behind the skull, above the ventral contact line.
Rear travelling wave rises while the anterior cervical junction remains the body root; not the crest of the tail wave.
High rear wave: low ventral cervical junction under the skull; raised tail is excluded from root measurement.
Tail tip lifts: anterior neck junction anchors the body, not the lifted tail or its changing silhouette extent.
Second-row prone pose: posterior skull/ventral cervical junction, same anatomical rule as move frame0.
Large rear wave: the cervical junction in front of the wave anchors the low forward body.
Small rear wave: anterior cervical junction remains the root, independent of tail flexion.
Wave returns to prone: ventral cervical junction behind the skull; tail crosses nominal cell edge but does not determine root.
Anticipation coil: lower anterior trunk loop supports the retracted head; track this load-bearing body section rather than the folded skull.
Neck rises: root at the lower upright forebody bend, above the ventral ground contact.
Jaw opens: lower cervical column base; open mandible and raised skull remain free to move above this root.
Forward strike: lower ventral S-bend is the supporting anterior trunk root. Do not lock the extended head; its rightward displacement is intentionally preserved.
Maximum extension: lower S-bend supports the outstretched forebody; the head and its proven right-cell spill remain uncut and offset to the right of this root.
Recoil S: lower anterior trunk coil remains grounded while the upper neck retracts; partly curved anatomy gives medium landmark confidence.
Return to low pose: visible ventral cervical junction behind the skull restores the same landmark used by locomotion.
Final low recovery: anterior cervical junction anchors the body independently of the extended tail.
Initial raised body: lower upright cervical/trunk bend at ventral ground contact, allowing the head to fall relative to the root.
Folded collapse: lower supporting anterior trunk loop is visible below the folded neck; track that body section despite partly occluded cervical anatomy.
Unfolding collapse: lower forebody bend immediately behind the descending neck; head remains free to rotate downward.
Prone collapse: ventral cervical junction behind the grounded skull; no tail-bounds recentering.
Settled prone pose: posterior skull/neck junction on the forward body, ignoring the flattened tail midpoint.
Small settling wave: same posterior skull/ventral neck junction; rear body settling must not drag the root.
Final settling wave: ventral cervical junction behind the skull maintains the forward-body root.
Final corpse: ventral cervical junction under the rear skull, preserved as a physical body marker without redrawing occluded anatomy.
